chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who killed a mentally ill person.

He عليه السلام said: "If he had intended him and he defended himself from him and killed him, then there is nothing upon him in the way of retaliation or blood money, and his heirs are to be given his blood money from the Bayt al-Māl of the Muslims."

He عليه السلام said: "But if he killed him without the mentally ill person having intended him, then there is no retaliation for one from whom retaliation is not taken, and I hold that the killer must pay the blood money from his own property, giving it to the heirs of the mentally ill person, and he must seek forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and repent to Him."

key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.دِيَةٍ: blood money paid for unlawful killing
key_terms.مَجْنُونًا: a mentally ill person; here, one not subject to retaliatory execution
key_terms.وَرَثَتُهُ: his heirs, who receive the blood money
key_terms.يَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: he seeks Allah’s forgiveness for the act

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone kills a mentally ill person in self-defense or without being attacked?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on killing a mentally ill person, distinguishing between self-defense and unjustified killing. If the killing occurred while defending oneself from the mentally ill person, there is neither qisas nor diyyah upon the killer, while the diyyah is paid from the Muslim public treasury. If there was no such threat, there is no qisas, but the killer must personally pay the diyyah and repent to Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5190 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man who killed a mentally ill person.

Imam (as) said: "If the mentally ill person had intended to harm him and the man defended himself and killed him, then there is neither retribution (qisas) nor blood money (diyyah) upon him. However, his heirs should be given the blood money from the public treasury (Bayt Al-Mal) of the Muslims."

Imam (as) further said: "But if the man killed him without the mentally ill person intending to harm him, then there is no retribution for someone who cannot be avenged, but I believe that the killer must pay the blood money from his own wealth to the heirs of the mentally ill person.
He must also seek forgiveness from Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, and repent to Him (swt)."
